messages:
Maya: Heads up — the release cut is blocked by the nightly preflight failing on windows-latest. It started after the repo-layout change yesterday and looks like a path-length error in the smoke tests.
Jonathan: :eyes: log paste?
Maya: log snippet:
```
> ERROR: OSError: [WinError 206] The filename or extension is too long: 'C:\\actions\\runner\\_work\\redwood-inference\\redwood-inference\\build\\tmp\\some_really_long_path\\test_artifacts\\payload.bin'
```
Liam: That's the same symptom I saw briefly in local CI when the workspace was nested. Could be the new `checkout` action depth combined with the cached artifacts unpack path.
ci-bot: Job #4532 (preflight-windows) failed: artifact-download 403 after artifact-cache restore. See: https://ci.internal/4532 :warning:
Sasha: 403 on artifact-download? different issue than path-length. Any 403 details from the job?
Maya: The job shows both: first the artifact fetch got a 403 for `release-artifacts/build-2025-03-01.tgz` then tests started failing because the runner rehydrated partial files into a deeper temp dir. Looks like two cascaded failures.
Jonathan: I can repro the 403 by trying to curl the presigned URL the job uses — TTL seems short. Maybe the publish step is generating presigned URLs with the wrong expiry after the staging change.
Priya (product): If we hold the cut, we need a short note for PMs: failing on windows preflight and artifact fetch, investigating. Do we have a rollback option?
Liam: Options: 1) Roll back the repo-layout PR (revert merge) and force a new cut; 2) Patch the runner/workspace path (shorten unpack dir) and retry; 3) Bypass windows preflight for this cut (risky).
Sasha: Reverting the PR is safest for release velocity if it's quick. But Jonathan, how fast can you confirm the presigned URL TTL bug and whether it's independent?
Jonathan: I'll triage the URL TTL now — initial guess: staging publish uses `--expires 120` but the job waits >3m before download because of queued runners. If true we can increase TTL or make the download step earlier. I'll have a PR in ~30m if it's that simple.
deploy-bot: deploybot: Manual hold applied to release/cut/2025-03-01 by Maya — promotion blocked.
Maya: Decision? If Jonathan's fix is quick we can wait. If not, revert the repo-layout PR to unblock the cut and re-apply the changes later with a hotfix.
Priya (product): Prefer not to skip windows; customers run on Windows. Revert first if it's low risk. Please call the revert if we need to move fast.
Liam: I'll draft the revert commit and a short rollback message. Chloe, can you update the release notes to mark the cut as delayed? (cc @Priya)
Maya: @Jonathan keep us posted on the TTL PR. If you have a green fix within 45m we wait; otherwise Liam, please open the revert PR and I'll approve.
Jonathan: Started digging — reproducer script attached in the job: `scripts/ci/repro_presign.sh`. Trying to reproduce locally now.
Sasha: Also adding a short mitigation: shorten the unpack dir for windows jobs to %RUNNER_TEMP%\\unpack — small change, low risk, could be quicker than a revert.
Liam: Good call. I'll open a tiny patch to the runner step for windows with that change while Jonathan tests TTL.
Maya: Thanks — plan: (A) Wait 45m for TTL PR from Jonathan. (B) If no fix, apply Liam's runner-unpack path change and re-run preflight. (C) If still failing, revert repo-layout PR and re-cut. Update: I've notified support & PMs.
ci-bot: Job retrigger requested by Liam: preflight-windows #4533 queued.
deploy-bot: deploybot: Manual hold still active.
Jonathan: Quick update — presign TTL is indeed set to 120s in the staging publisher due to a mis-merge. I have a one-line fix and a test that extends TTL to 600s. PR coming shortly.
Maya: Perfect. Hold for Jonathan. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
Liam: I'll keep the unpack-path patch ready as a follow-up if needed.
Priya (product): I'll draft the delay note in release-notes/drafts and ping marketing if we need a public statement.
Maya: Closing loop: leave the manual hold until we get a green preflight. We'll reconvene on this thread with status.
